findings.summary: Discrete-event simulation literature treats equal-time non-commutative events as requiring an explicit total ordering/tie policy for determinism. NESTML likewise documents that exactly simultaneous pre/post synaptic events are order-sensitive and fixes post-before-pre processing in the reference/default generated code.
sources: NESTML active dendrite third-factor STDP tutorial, Case 7

findings.summary: NEST spike_generator explicitly interprets repeated identical times as multiple events, while mip_generator can collapse n same-step spikes into one event with n-fold weight. Multiplicity/aggregation is therefore an ordinary declared event representation, not something that should silently inherit host-language iterable order.

NESTML stdp_nn_symm_synapse discards exactly coincident zero-delta-t pairs, demonstrating that discard, explicit order and multiplicity are all legitimate model-defined policies. There is no universal exact-tie semantics to infer from simultaneity alone.

Foundational event-driven spiking/dynamical-synapse work treats events as state-transition points. SparkBrain v0.5 updates receptor traces and adaptive gain after each pulse, so any future exact-key permutation effect is first explained by sequential state jumps under an unspecified tie policy.
sources: Mattia & Del Giudice, Neural Computation 2000, DOI 10.1162/089976600300014953
